standard_prerequisites.name: The pebble game on a poset
standard_prerequisites.statement: An algorithm that keeps a number of pebbles on each vertex and accepts edges while respecting the sparsity parameters, with a reachability operation used to move pebbles along accepted edges.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the algorithm whose behaviour the statement describes.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pebble, span and out counts
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a subset of vertices the number of pebbles, the span and the out-degree are related to the weighted size of the classes the subset meets by the algorithm's invariants.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the quantities used to count pebbles inside a reachable set.

standard_prerequisites.name: Reachable set of a vertex
standard_prerequisites.statement: The set of vertices that can be reached from a given vertex by following accepted edges, respecting the direction conventions of the game.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the set on which the counting argument is performed.

core_obligations: Split into the case where the two endpoints together carry more than the parameter number of pebbles, in which the edge can simply be added and a pebble removed, and the complementary case (source line 919).

In the complementary case form the union of the reachable sets of the two endpoints and use the algorithm's invariant to express the sum of the span and the pebble count over that set as the weighted size of the classes it meets (source lines 920-923).

Rearrange to obtain that the pebble count over that union exceeds the parameter, so that some vertex of the union other than the two endpoints still carries a pebble, and that vertex, being reachable, allows the pebble to be brought back and the edge to be accepted (source lines 925-928).

proof_roadmap.step: The case of many pebbles at the two endpoints.
Counting pebbles in the union of the reachable sets.
Find the spare vertex and accept the edge.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 913-917: given parameters satisfying the numbered inequalities, if after some steps of the algorithm all accepted edges lie between two consecutive vertex classes, then an edge between vertices of those classes that is not yet accepted can be accepted or moved. The proof (source lines 918-929) separates the case where the two endpoints together carry more than the parameter number of pebbles, where the edge can be accepted at once, from the complementary case, and in the latter it forms the union of the reachable sets of the two endpoints, uses the algorithm's invariant to identify the sum of span and pebbles on that union with the weighted size of the classes it meets, and deduces that some vertex other than the endpoints still holds a pebble, which, being reachable, can be brought back. The statement records the possibility of the move and neither the reachability set nor the counting invariant.
